key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while multitask neural networks provided strong shared-task generalization.
engineering_relevance: For welding process optimization, the study shows that predictive models can support faster quality assessment of joint strength and hardness without relying solely on exhaustive testing.
method: Compared multitask neural networks (shared hidden layers, task-specific outputs) with stacking ensemble learning.
Used a shared dataset to predict three welding properties: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated both approaches using RMSE and R² across all tasks.
evidence_signal: MTNN achieved RMSE/R² of 0.1288/0.6724 for UTS, 0.0886/0.9215 for weld hardness, and 0.1125/0.8407 for HAZ hardness, while stacking improved to 0.0263/0.9863, 0.0467/0.9782, and 0.1109/0.8453 respectively.
watch_item: Performance may depend on dataset size and task coupling; stacking can outperform on accuracy but may be less efficient and less transferable than shared multitask models.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
